title: Absorb the loss of your biggest customer
summary: Your biggest customer is leaving. Get the real reason first; a budget cut, a lost champion, a product gap, and an acquisition are different problems with different saves. Read the agreement before the next call: notice and renewal mechanics, committed payments, and transition obligations run on the contract's clock, not yours. Size the hole: the customer's share of revenue, the runway on the new numbers, and the cost actions each scenario triggers. Make one disciplined save attempt with an executive sponsor and a concession you can honor. Tell the board and investors yourself, with the concentration number and the plan; most investor agreements carry information rights (the NVCA model documents show the standard shape), and the story travels faster than the board deck. Then replan the pipeline: the gap is a quota, and the next deals should respect a concentration ceiling so one logo cannot repeat this. Educational guidance, not legal advice.

parts.title: Get the real reason from the economic buyer: a budget cut, a lost champion, a product gap, and an acquisition are different problems

execution.rationale: The founder speaks directly with the economic buyer and the champion to learn why the account is leaving and records what is known without guessing motives.

parts.title: Read the agreement before the next call: notice and renewal mechanics, committed payments, termination-for-convenience terms, and transition obligations

execution.rationale: Extract the notice, renewal, committed-payment, and transition clauses from the supplied customer agreement for the founder's and counsel's review.

parts.title: Size the hole: the customer's share of revenue, the runway on the new numbers, and the cost actions each scenario triggers

execution.rationale: Recompute revenue concentration, runway, and spending scenarios from the supplied revenue-by-customer and accounting records.

parts.title: Make one disciplined save attempt: an executive sponsor and a concession package you can actually honor

execution.rationale: The founder or executive sponsor runs the save conversation directly with the customer and decides what concession the company can honor.

parts.title: If the save lands on changed terms, negotiate the renewal agreement properly rather than concede by email
parts.when: The save attempt lands on changed terms

execution.rationale: The founder and counsel negotiate and paper the changed commercial terms with the customer's team.

parts.title: Tell the board and investors yourself: the concentration number, the plan, and whatever your information-rights agreements require

references.title: NVCA model legal documents (investor information rights)

execution.rationale: The founder personally updates the board and investors on the lost account, the revenue-concentration picture, and the replacement plan.

parts.title: Start the cost actions the scenario math triggered, now rather than after two optimistic quarters

execution.rationale: Draft the cost scenarios and implementation priorities from current spending for management's decisions.

parts.title: Replan the pipeline to refill the gap: coverage targets, a restarted outbound motion, and a concentration ceiling the next deals respect

execution.rationale: Recompute pipeline coverage against the lost revenue and build the named-account target list from the CRM export; the outbound restart runs as its own process.

metadata.trigger: Your biggest customer gives notice: non-renewal, termination for convenience, or an acquisition that ends the account your revenue leans on.
metadata.supportReason: The reason-finding, the save attempt, and the board conversation are founder work; an agent can read the agreement's notice and renewal terms, size the concentration and runway scenarios, and rebuild the pipeline targets from the CRM.

contextNeeded.query: the customer agreement (notice, renewal, termination, and committed-payment terms)
revenue by customer, plus current cash and burn
